meta.fxNote: USD conversions in this guide assume approximately VND 26,000 = US$1. The rate moves. Treat every dollar figure as an order of magnitude, not a quote, and check the rate on the day you move money.
meta.tagline: Every legal route from the USA to Vietnam, as one decision tree. Including the routes that do not exist.

realityCheck.claim: Vietnam has a golden visa I can buy.
realityCheck.reality: It does not, as of the verification date of this guide. A 5-to-10-year 'golden visa' was proposed to the Prime Minister by the Tourism Advisory Board in 2025 and has been widely reported as if it were live. There is no decree number and no application channel. Some sites cite a 'Resolution 41/2026/QH15' pilot; no Vietnamese government source confirms that resolution exists, and the outlets carrying the claim sell visa services.
realityCheck.why: Golden-visa search traffic is extremely valuable to agencies. Reporting a proposal as a program generates leads years before any program exists.

realityCheck.claim: Americans get 45 days visa-free like the Brits and the Europeans do.
realityCheck.reality: No. Vietnam's unilateral visa exemption covers roughly two dozen countries. The United States is not one of them. Americans need a visa for every single entry, including a weekend trip. The practical default is the 90-day e-visa.
realityCheck.why: Blog posts written for a UK or EU audience get syndicated and rewritten without the nationality caveat.

realityCheck.claim: There is a digital nomad visa, or a retirement visa.
realityCheck.reality: Vietnam has neither. There is no visa category for a remote worker paid by a foreign company, and no category for a retiree living on passive income. The new UĐ1 tech visa is not a nomad visa: it runs through a Vietnamese employer, university, or research body, which excludes freelancers and remote employees of foreign firms.
realityCheck.why: Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines all launched nomad or retirement visas. Writers assume Vietnam followed. It did not.

realityCheck.claim: I'll just open a company and that gets me residency.
realityCheck.reality: Only above a capital threshold. Contributing under VND 3 billion (roughly US$115,000) puts you in the DT4 tier, which grants a visa of up to 12 months and no temporary residence card. You will have a Vietnamese company, ongoing accounting and tax obligations, and still no residence card. The residence card starts at DT3, meaning VND 3 billion or more actually contributed.
realityCheck.why: Company formation agencies earn their fee at incorporation. The residency outcome is the customer's problem afterwards.

realityCheck.claim: Working online for my US clients from a Vietnamese tourist visa is fine, everyone does it.
realityCheck.reality: It is prohibited on paper and tolerated in practice, and those are two different risks. Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence bars foreigners from labour activities on a tourist entry; administrative fines run VND 15–25 million (roughly US$600–1,000). Enforcement against people quietly serving foreign clients has been close to nonexistent. That is a tolerance, not a right, and it can be withdrawn without notice. Decide with open eyes; do not let anyone tell you it is legal.
realityCheck.why: Everyone's lived experience is that nothing happened to them. Survivorship bias reads as legal advice.

realityCheck.claim: The US and Vietnam have a tax treaty, so I won't be double taxed.
realityCheck.reality: A treaty was signed in July 2015 and Vietnam ratified it in 2017, but the US Senate never did, so it has never entered into force. There are no treaty tie-breaker rules for dual residency and no reduced withholding. Your entire defense against double taxation is the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and the Foreign Tax Credit.
realityCheck.why: The treaty was signed with fanfare in 2015 and the announcement articles still rank well. Almost nobody publishes the non-ratification follow-up.

nodes.question: How long do you need to be in Vietnam, and will you be paid by a Vietnamese entity?
nodes.help: Answer for the stay you actually want, not the one you think you can get. Almost every expensive mistake in Vietnamese immigration comes from someone entering on a short-stay permission and then trying to convert it into a life.

answers.label: 90 days or less, and no Vietnamese employer or Vietnamese clients
answers.note: This is a visit, and the answer is simple.

answers.label: Longer than 90 days, or I will be paid by a Vietnamese entity
answers.note: This is a move. Keep going.

nodes.question: Do you have a Vietnamese family connection?
nodes.help: This is the first question for a reason. A Vietnamese family connection is by a wide margin the cheapest and most durable route, and many Americans with a Vietnamese parent or grandparent do not realise they qualify for anything. Check this before you consider paying for a company.

answers.label: I held Vietnamese nationality, or I have a Vietnamese parent or grandparent
answers.note: You are 'Viet Kieu' for these purposes.

answers.label: I am married to a Vietnamese citizen
answers.note: Two options open up: the 5-year exemption certificate and the TT residence card.

nodes.question: Do you have a Vietnamese employer — or the Vietnamese entity of a foreign employer — willing to sponsor you?
nodes.help: Sponsorship is not a favour, it is paperwork the company must file in its own name. A company with no Vietnamese legal entity cannot sponsor you no matter how much it wants to. Ask specifically: 'Does the entity that will file my work permit have a Vietnamese business registration certificate?'

answers.label: No, but I am a senior digital-technology professional who could be sponsored by a Vietnamese company, university, or research institute
answers.note: A route that only opened on 1 July 2026.

nodes.question: Do you meet the expert test — a university degree or equivalent, plus relevant experience of 2 years, or 1 year in priority technology, innovation, and digital-transformation sectors?
nodes.help: Decree 219/2025 cut the standard experience requirement from 3 years to 2, and to 1 year in priority sectors. Your degree does not have to match the job title exactly, but the closer it matches the job description your employer files, the smoother the approval.

answers.label: No, but I am an intra-company transferee — employed by the foreign parent 12+ months and moving to its Vietnamese presence
No, or I am not sure
answers.note: Have your employer check the exemption list before you give up on this branch — there are roughly 15 to 20 exemption categories.

nodes.question: How much capital can you contribute to a Vietnamese company in your own name, and leave in place?
nodes.help: This is contributed charter capital that is actually transferred and registered, not a bank balance you show once and take home. The tier you land in determines whether you get a residence card at all. Assume roughly VND 26,000 to US$1.

answers.label: VND 3 to 50 billion (about US$115k to 1.9M)
answers.note: This is the lowest tier that produces a residence card.

nodes.question: Are you enrolling in a Vietnamese university, degree program, or full-time accredited language program?
nodes.help: Full-time enrolment at an institution licensed to host foreign students. A part-time evening Vietnamese class at a private language centre generally will not sponsor a DH visa.

answers.label: Yes, I have or can get an admission letter

nodes.question: Which of these describes you?
nodes.help: You have reached the part of the tree where Vietnam has no category built for you. What follows is the honest answer, not a workaround dressed up as a pathway.

answers.label: I am retired or living on passive income
I work remotely for a non-Vietnamese employer or clients

nodes.verdict: Under VND 3 billion you are in the DT4 tier: a visa of up to 12 months and no temporary residence card. You will hold a Vietnamese company with real accounting, tax, and reporting duties, and you will still be renewing short-term permission to stay. This is the single most common way Americans waste US$5,000 to 15,000 in agency and formation fees in Vietnam.
alternatives: Reach VND 3 billion in genuinely contributed capital and enter at DT3, which does carry a residence card of up to 3 years.
Use the company as a business decision on its own merits, and solve residence separately through employment.
If your business does not actually need to be Vietnamese, keep the entity at home and reconsider whether you need long-term residence at all.

nodes.verdict: Vietnam has no retirement visa. There is no category based on age, pension, passive income, or property purchase. Buying an apartment grants you no immigration status whatsoever.
alternatives: Rolling 90-day e-visas with exits. Legal for presence, but it is a permanent state of leaving, and each new e-visa is a fresh discretionary decision by immigration.
If you have a Vietnamese spouse or Vietnamese ancestry, go back to the family branch — it is the only stable low-cost route.
Invest at DT3 level or above if you have the capital and want the company anyway.
Compare against neighbours before committing: Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines all run retirement categories Vietnam does not.

nodes.verdict: There is no visa in Vietnam for a remote worker paid from abroad. The 90-day multiple-entry e-visa is what almost every remote worker in Vietnam actually uses, and doing paid work on it is prohibited by Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law with fines of VND 15–25 million. Enforcement against people serving foreign clients has been close to nonexistent, but you are relying on tolerance, not on a right.
alternatives: Rolling 90-day e-visas, with a clear understanding of the legal position you are accepting.
Get hired by a Vietnamese entity, including a local subsidiary of a foreign firm, and take the work permit route — the only clean answer.
Contribute VND 3 billion or more to your own Vietnamese company and take DT3 with a residence card, if the business is real.
If you are senior in digital technology, look hard at whether a Vietnamese employer, university, or research institute would sponsor you for UĐ1.

nodes.verdict: On the facts you have given, no long-term Vietnamese immigration category currently fits you. That is a real answer and it is better to have it now than after spending money.
alternatives: Change one input rather than looking for a loophole: acquire a sponsor, acquire capital, or enrol in a program.
Use 90-day e-visas to spend real time in Vietnam and build the connection that produces a sponsor.
Re-run this tree after any change in employment, marriage, or capital — the answer flips entirely on those inputs.

pathways.name: 90-Day E-Visa
pathways.summary: Vietnam's default entry permission for Americans: fully online, up to 90 days, available single or multiple entry. This is the tool you will use for scouting trips, and the one most long-stayers quietly live on.
pathways.bestFor: Scouting trips, the gap between arriving and having a work permit approved, and anyone who has not yet triggered a long-term category.
pathways.renewable: Not extended in the ordinary case — you apply for a new one. Practice varies and in-country extension is not something to plan around.
pathways.canBringFamily: Each person applies separately, including children.
pathways.canWorkLocally: No. Labour activity on a tourist entry is prohibited under Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law.

eligibility.requirement: US passport valid at least 6 months beyond entry
eligibility.detail: Count from your intended entry date, not your application date.

eligibility.requirement: Passport-standard digital photo and a scan of the passport bio page
eligibility.detail: Plain white background, no glasses, face fully visible. Photo rejection is the most common cause of a failed application.

eligibility.requirement: A declared port of entry
eligibility.detail: You must name the checkpoint you will physically use, and it must match on arrival.

costs.note: Official government fee. Non-refundable, including when your own typo causes the rejection.
Worth it for anyone who will leave and return within the 90 days.

pathways.timeline: 3 to 5 working days standard. Apply at least two weeks before departure so you can survive one rejection and reapply.

steps.title: Apply on the official government portal only
steps.detail: Vietnam's national e-visa portal is a government site. Dozens of commercial sites clone its look and charge US$50 to 90 for the same US$25 application. Confirm you are on a .gov.vn domain before you pay.

steps.title: Enter your name exactly as machine-readable on your passport
steps.detail: Surname and given names in the same fields the passport uses. A middle name in the wrong box is a rejection.
steps.blocker: Have the passport physically in front of you.

steps.title: Choose the correct entry port
steps.detail: If you might fly into Tan Son Nhat but could reroute to Noi Bai, this matters. See the gotcha on port matching.

steps.title: Pay and save the registration code
steps.detail: The code is how you retrieve the visa. Without it, recovery is painful.

steps.title: Download and print the approved e-visa
steps.detail: Carry a paper copy. Airline check-in staff at US airports frequently ask to see it before boarding, and phone batteries die.

failureModes.mistake: Applying through a lookalike commercial site
failureModes.consequence: You pay two to four times the official fee, and sometimes get a visa-on-arrival letter you did not want.
failureModes.avoid: Verify the domain ends in .gov.vn before entering card details.

failureModes.mistake: Arriving at a different port than declared
failureModes.consequence: Refused entry at the border, with the airline liable to fly you back.
failureModes.avoid: If your routing changes, apply for a new e-visa with the correct port.

failureModes.mistake: Treating the 90 days as renewable in-country
failureModes.consequence: Overstay, fines, and a border record that makes every future application harder.
failureModes.avoid: Book the exit before you enter.

verification.check: That you are on the official portal, and that the fee is US$25 single or US$50 multiple
verification.how: Type evisa.gov.vn into the address bar directly — never arrive from a search ad. Check the fee at the payment screen before entering card details.
verification.expectAnswer: The domain ends in .gov.vn and the total matches US$25 or US$50. Anything higher means you are on a reseller and should close the tab.

verification.check: That your declared port of entry matches the airport on your ticket
verification.how: Put your booking confirmation next to the application form and compare the arrival airport against the port you select.
verification.expectAnswer: An exact match. If your itinerary later changes airports, you need a new e-visa, not an amendment.

pathways.name: 5-Year Visa Exemption Certificate
pathways.summary: The best-value document in Vietnamese immigration, and the least known. For people of Vietnamese origin and the foreign spouses and children of Vietnamese citizens: five years of unlimited entries, up to 180 days per entry, no visa fee each time.
pathways.bestFor: Americans with a Vietnamese parent or grandparent, former Vietnamese nationals, and foreign spouses of Vietnamese citizens who do not need to work locally.
pathways.durationGranted: 5 years, capped at 180 days per single entry. Cannot exceed remaining passport validity.
pathways.renewable: Yes, reapply on the same basis.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: Not directly, but it coexists with other applications and takes the pressure off completely.
pathways.canBringFamily: Spouse and children apply on the family relationship, each with their own certificate.
pathways.canWorkLocally: No — it is an entry exemption, not a work authorisation. Working still requires a work permit or a documented exemption.

eligibility.requirement: Passport valid at least 1 year
eligibility.detail: Longer is better; the certificate cannot outlast the passport.

eligibility.requirement: Proof of Vietnamese origin, or proof of family relationship to a Vietnamese citizen
eligibility.detail: For Viet Kieu: a decision permitting relinquishment of Vietnamese nationality, a certificate of loss of nationality, an old Vietnamese ID card (even expired), a household registration book, or a birth records extract. For spouses and children: marriage or birth certificate plus the Vietnamese relative's identity documents.

costs.note: Set by the issuing mission. Confirm with the embassy or consulate handling your application.
For Viet Kieu whose family left decades ago, finding the proof is the whole cost of this pathway. Budget time, not just money.

pathways.timeline: Typically a few weeks once you hold the proof documents. Finding the proof documents can take months.

steps.title: Establish which proof of origin you can actually obtain
steps.detail: Work backwards from what exists: a parent's Vietnamese birth certificate, an old household registration book, a relinquishment-of-nationality decision. Ask the oldest relative in the family first — this is where the documents usually are.

steps.title: Get foreign-issued documents apostilled
steps.detail: US marriage and birth certificates used as proof need authentication. From 11 September 2026 this is an apostille rather than consular legalization — see the gotcha, the timing matters right now.

steps.title: Have documents translated into Vietnamese and notarised
steps.detail: Use a translation office that routinely serves immigration filings.

steps.title: File with the Vietnamese embassy or consulate, or with Immigration inside Vietnam
steps.detail: US-based applicants normally file with the Embassy in Washington DC or the Consulate General in San Francisco or Houston.
steps.where: Vietnamese diplomatic mission, or Vietnam Immigration Department

steps.title: Collect the certificate and check every field
steps.detail: Verify the name spelling and validity dates before you leave the counter. Corrections later are a new application.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming you do not qualify because you were born in the US and speak no Vietnamese
failureModes.consequence: You spend US$10,000 on a company you did not need.
failureModes.avoid: Vietnamese origin runs through ancestry and former nationality, not language or birthplace. Check before you dismiss it.

failureModes.mistake: Letting the certificate outrun the passport
failureModes.consequence: The certificate is issued short, or invalidated when you renew the passport.
failureModes.avoid: Renew the US passport first if it has under two years left.

failureModes.mistake: Treating 180 days per entry as 180 days per year
failureModes.consequence: Overstay.
failureModes.avoid: The clock resets on each entry, but each stay is capped. Track entry dates.

verification.check: Whether the specific proof of Vietnamese origin you hold is sufficient
verification.authority: Vietnamese Embassy in Washington DC, or the Consulate General in San Francisco or Houston
verification.how: Email the consular section listing exactly what you have — for example "my mother’s Vietnamese birth certificate and her expired Vietnamese ID, but no relinquishment-of-nationality decision" — and ask whether that set supports a 5-year visa exemption certificate.
verification.expectAnswer: A yes or no that names your documents. "Bring whatever you have" is not an answer — reply asking them to confirm the specific set.

verification.check: The current fee and processing time at the mission handling your case
verification.how: Ask in the same email. Fees are set per mission and the published figures online are frequently stale.

pathways.name: TT Family Visa and 3-Year Residence Card
pathways.summary: The residence route for foreign spouses, children, and parents of Vietnamese citizens. Produces a temporary residence card valid up to 3 years, which functions as a multiple-entry visa substitute.
pathways.bestFor: Americans married to Vietnamese citizens who want a stable base rather than a rolling permission.
pathways.durationGranted: TT residence card up to 3 years
pathways.renewable: Yes, on continuing relationship and valid passport.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: Permanent residence exists for spouses of Vietnamese citizens after a qualifying period of continuous temporary residence. Treat it as a long-horizon goal and take specific legal advice — the qualifying rules are strict and periodically amended.
pathways.canBringFamily: Children of the marriage are covered on the same family basis.
pathways.canWorkLocally: The card itself is not work authorisation. However, being married to a Vietnamese citizen and residing in Vietnam has historically been one of the work permit exemption categories. Confirm your status under Decree 219/2025 with your employer or a licensed adviser before you start work — do not assume it carried over unchanged.

eligibility.requirement: Marriage registered and recognised in Vietnam
eligibility.detail: A marriage performed abroad must be recorded in Vietnam, or evidenced by a legalised or apostilled consular note of the registration.

eligibility.requirement: Passport with at least 13 months validity
eligibility.detail: The card must expire at least 30 days before the passport does, so short passports produce short cards.

eligibility.requirement: Entry on a visa consistent with family purpose
eligibility.detail: You generally need to be in Vietnam on a TT visa, sponsored by your Vietnamese spouse, before the card application. Entering on an e-visa and converting is not reliable.

eligibility.requirement: Vietnamese spouse's identity and residence documents
eligibility.detail: Certified copies of the national ID or citizen identity card and household registration.

costs.amount: Roughly US$145 to 320 depending on validity
costs.note: Renewals and extensions are far cheaper, around US$10. Confirm current fees at filing.

costs.item: Apostille or legalization plus certified translation
costs.note: Depends on how many US documents you need and which state issued them.
Genuinely optional on this route if your Vietnamese spouse can attend the offices with you.

pathways.timeline: Plan 2 to 4 months from starting document collection to card in hand. Card processing itself is 5 to 10 working days once filed.

steps.title: Register or record the marriage so Vietnam recognises it
steps.detail: If you married in the US, this is the step that gates everything else. Get the marriage certificate apostilled, translated, and recorded.
steps.blocker: Nothing else can proceed until the marriage is documented Vietnamese-side.

steps.title: Your Vietnamese spouse sponsors your TT visa
steps.detail: The sponsorship is filed by the Vietnamese citizen, not by you.

steps.title: Enter Vietnam on the TT visa
steps.detail: Enter on the family-purpose visa, not on an e-visa, so the residence card application is consistent.

steps.title: Complete temporary residence declaration at your address
steps.detail: Within 12 hours of arriving at the accommodation. Your landlord or spouse files it. See the gotcha — this trips up more people than any other single rule.

steps.title: File the residence card application
steps.detail: Form, photos at 3x4cm on white background taken within 6 months, passport, marriage and family documents, spouse's ID and household registration.

failureModes.mistake: Relying on a US marriage certificate that was never recorded in Vietnam
failureModes.consequence: Application refused; months lost.
failureModes.avoid: Record the marriage first, then everything else.

failureModes.mistake: Applying with a passport that has under 13 months left
failureModes.consequence: You get a short card or a refusal, and pay again next year.
failureModes.avoid: Renew the passport before you file.

failureModes.mistake: Starting work on the strength of the card alone
failureModes.consequence: Illegal employment exposure for you and your employer.
failureModes.avoid: Get the work permit, or get the exemption confirmed in writing under Decree 219/2025.

verification.check: Whether your US marriage must be recorded in Vietnam before you can apply
verification.authority: The People’s Committee (Ủy ban nhân dân) of your spouse’s district
verification.how: Have your Vietnamese spouse attend or phone their district office and ask what is required to record a marriage registered abroad, and what the recorded certificate is called.
verification.expectAnswer: A named document and a list of what to bring. This is the step that gates everything else, so get it in concrete terms.

verification.check: Whether marriage to a Vietnamese citizen still exempts you from a work permit under Decree 219/2025
verification.authority: Your provincial labour authority, via a written enquiry
verification.how: Ask, in writing, which article of Decree 219/2025 covers spouses of Vietnamese citizens, and whether a written exemption confirmation is still required before starting work.
verification.expectAnswer: An article reference. See the contested-claims section — do not act on a verbal yes.

pathways.name: Work Permit, LĐ Visa, and 2-Year Residence Card
pathways.summary: The main road. Your employer obtains a work permit under Decree 219/2025, which supports an LĐ visa and then a temporary residence card aligned to the permit. Decree 219 made this materially faster than it was before August 2025.
pathways.bestFor: Anyone with a genuine Vietnamese employer, including local subsidiaries of American companies, schools, and universities.
pathways.durationGranted: Work permit up to 2 years; residence card aligned to it and capped at 2 years.
pathways.renewable: Yes. Start renewal well before expiry — the card cannot outlast the permit.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: Not directly, but continuous lawful residence is the foundation for any later permanent residence application.
pathways.canBringFamily: Yes — spouse and children under 18 on TT dependant status, sponsored by you once you hold the card.
pathways.canWorkLocally: Yes, for the sponsoring employer, in the position named on the permit. The permit is job-specific and employer-specific.

eligibility.requirement: A Vietnamese legal entity willing to sponsor
eligibility.detail: The entity files in its own name. No entity, no permit.

eligibility.requirement: Expert test: degree or equivalent plus 2 years relevant experience
eligibility.detail: Reduced to 1 year for priority sectors — science, technology, innovation, and national digital transformation. Down from 3 years under the old Decree 152/2020 regime.

eligibility.requirement: Criminal record check issued within the last 6 months
eligibility.detail: For Americans this is normally the FBI Identity History Summary. The 6-month clock is the single most common sequencing failure on this pathway.

eligibility.requirement: Health certificate
eligibility.detail: Issued by a hospital recognised for this purpose. In practice, done in Vietnam after arrival, at a licensed international or provincial hospital.

eligibility.requirement: Authenticated degree and professional certificates
eligibility.detail: US-issued diplomas must be authenticated and translated. From 11 September 2026, apostille replaces consular legalization for documents from the US.

costs.note: Set at provincial level and varies. Usually paid by the employer.

costs.item: FBI Identity History Summary plus channeler
costs.amount: US$18 government fee, US$50 to 100 via an approved channeler
costs.note: The channeler is worth it — turnaround drops from weeks to days.

costs.item: Apostille on degree and criminal record
costs.amount: US$20 to 200 depending on issuing authority and expediting
costs.note: Federal documents such as the FBI summary are apostilled by the US Department of State; state-issued documents by that state's Secretary of State.
Most employers with foreign staff already have a firm and absorb this.

pathways.timeline: Under Decree 219/2025, the work permit itself is a single 10-working-day process, replacing the old two-stage sequence of job position approval plus permit. Realistically, 8 to 14 weeks door to door, because document authentication in the US dominates the schedule.

steps.title: Secure the offer and confirm the entity can sponsor
steps.detail: Ask directly whether the hiring entity holds a Vietnamese business registration certificate and has filed work permits before.

steps.title: Order the FBI Identity History Summary — but time it deliberately
steps.detail: It must be less than 6 months old when the application is filed. Ordering it too early is as damaging as ordering it too late. Work backwards from your employer's filing date.

steps.title: Authenticate your degree and criminal record
steps.detail: From 11 September 2026, obtain an apostille rather than going through Vietnamese consular legalization. Federal documents go to the US Department of State; state-issued documents to the relevant Secretary of State.
steps.takes: 1 to 6 weeks depending on state and expediting

steps.title: Send authenticated documents to your employer for translation and filing
steps.detail: Your employer submits the work permit application under Decree 219/2025.

steps.title: Enter Vietnam and complete the health certificate
steps.detail: Done at a licensed hospital in Vietnam. Straightforward, half a day.

steps.title: Temporary residence declaration within 12 hours of reaching your accommodation
steps.detail: Filed by your landlord or hotel. Confirm it was actually done.

steps.title: Convert to the LĐ visa and apply for the residence card
steps.detail: The card is aligned to the work permit and must expire at least 30 days before your passport.

failureModes.mistake: Getting the FBI check apostilled 7 months before the employer files
failureModes.consequence: Rejected on document age. You reorder and re-authenticate, losing 4 to 6 weeks.
failureModes.avoid: Agree the filing date with your employer, then work backwards.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming the permit transfers when you change jobs
failureModes.consequence: You are working illegally from your first day at the new employer.
failureModes.avoid: The permit is employer-specific. A new employer files a new permit.

failureModes.mistake: Letting the residence card lapse while the permit is renewed
failureModes.consequence: A gap in lawful residence, which complicates every future application.
failureModes.avoid: Start renewal 60 days out. Do not wait for the employer to remember.

failureModes.mistake: Passport with under 2 years left
failureModes.consequence: Card issued short, so you repeat the whole exercise early.
failureModes.avoid: Renew the passport in the US before you move.

verification.check: The exact date your employer will submit the work permit dossier
verification.authority: Your employer’s HR or immigration counsel
verification.how: Ask literally: "On what date will you file my work permit dossier?" Then order your FBI check six to eight weeks before that date.
verification.expectAnswer: A calendar date. "Soon" is not usable — the criminal record check has a six-month shelf life and needs an anchor.

verification.check: Which form of document authentication the receiving office is accepting this month
verification.authority: The provincial office that will receive the dossier, and the Vietnam MOFA Consular Department
verification.how: Ask whether they are accepting apostilles under the Convention that entered into force for Vietnam on 11 September 2026, or still requiring consular legalization for US documents.
verification.expectAnswer: A clear statement of one or the other. During a transition, ask again a week before you order anything.

verification.check: That your degree and experience satisfy the expert test for the job title being filed
verification.authority: Provincial labour authority, via your employer
verification.how: Have your employer confirm the job title on the dossier and ask whether your degree field is accepted for it, and whether your sector qualifies for the reduced one-year experience threshold.
verification.expectAnswer: Confirmation against the filed job title, not against your CV in general.

pathways.name: Work Permit Exemption Confirmation
pathways.summary: Not everyone who works in Vietnam needs a work permit. Decree 219/2025 sets out roughly 15 to 20 exemption categories, and an exemption still requires a written confirmation from the labour authority. Skipping the confirmation because you 'are exempt' is itself a violation.
pathways.bestFor: Intra-company transferees, company owners and board members above capital thresholds, short assignments under 90 days in a calendar year, and spouses of Vietnamese citizens residing in Vietnam.
pathways.durationGranted: Confirmation up to 2 years, supporting a residence card of matching length.
pathways.canBringFamily: Yes, dependants on TT status once you hold a residence card.
pathways.canWorkLocally: Yes, within the scope of the exemption category and the entity named on it.

eligibility.requirement: You fall in a listed exemption category
eligibility.detail: Common ones for Americans: intra-company transfer after 12+ months with the foreign parent that has a commercial presence in Vietnam; owner or capital contributor of an LLC, or board member of a joint stock company, above the applicable capital threshold; total working time under 90 days in a calendar year; married to a Vietnamese citizen and residing in Vietnam. The list is defined by decree and was restated in Decree 219/2025 — have it checked against the current text for your exact facts.

eligibility.requirement: Written confirmation of exemption obtained before you start work
eligibility.detail: The exemption is a status you must be granted, not one you can assert.

costs.note: Usually handled and paid by the employer.
Same apostille and translation work as the full permit route, generally less of it.

pathways.timeline: Shorter than a full work permit, but do not assume it is instant — build in 4 to 8 weeks including document authentication.

steps.title: Identify the exact exemption category in the current decree
steps.detail: Have your employer's counsel name the specific clause. 'We think you're exempt' is not a filing.

steps.title: Assemble evidence for that specific category
steps.detail: Intra-company transfer needs employment history with the parent; capital-based exemptions need the investment registration and capital contribution evidence.

steps.title: File for the written exemption confirmation
steps.detail: Filed by the employer with the labour authority before work begins.

steps.title: Use the confirmation to obtain the visa and residence card
steps.detail: The confirmation plays the same role a work permit would in the residence card application.

failureModes.mistake: Working on the assumption of exemption without the confirmation
failureModes.consequence: Illegal employment for you and a fine for the employer, regardless of whether you genuinely qualified.
failureModes.avoid: No work before the paper exists.

failureModes.mistake: Relying on the under-90-days exemption repeatedly
failureModes.consequence: Decree 219 frames this as total working time under 90 days in one calendar year, not per trip. Repeat short trips add up.
failureModes.avoid: Track cumulative days across the calendar year.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming the pre-August-2025 exemption list still applies
failureModes.consequence: Filing under a repealed decree.
failureModes.avoid: Decree 219/2025 replaced Decree 152/2020 and its Decree 70/2023 amendments from 7 August 2025.

verification.check: The exact article and clause of Decree 219/2025 you are exempt under
verification.authority: Your employer’s immigration counsel, confirmed with the provincial labour authority
verification.how: Ask counsel to name the article and clause in writing. Then have the employer file for the written exemption confirmation citing it.
verification.expectAnswer: A specific article number. "You should be fine" is the answer that gets people fined.

verification.check: Whether your cumulative days this calendar year still fit the short-assignment exemption
verification.how: If relying on the under-90-days category, total every working day in Vietnam this calendar year, across all trips, and confirm the count is measured cumulatively rather than per trip.

pathways.name: UĐ1 Digital Technology Visa
pathways.summary: Vietnam's newest and longest standard visa, live since 1 July 2026 under Law 118/2025/QH15. Up to 5 years for high-quality digital technology personnel, with UĐ2 covering the spouse and children under 18.
pathways.bestFor: Senior software, AI, semiconductor, and digital infrastructure professionals who can attract a Vietnamese institutional sponsor.
pathways.durationGranted: Up to 5 years — the longest standard validity in the current framework.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: Not yet defined. The conversion route from UĐ1 status to a temporary residence card was still awaiting implementing regulations during 2026.
pathways.canBringFamily: Yes — that is exactly what UĐ2 is for.

eligibility.requirement: Recognised as high-quality personnel in the digital technology industry
eligibility.detail: The criteria run through an institution: a Vietnamese employer, a university, or a research body. This structurally excludes freelancers and remote employees of foreign companies.

eligibility.requirement: An institutional sponsor in Vietnam
eligibility.detail: As with the work permit, no sponsor means no application.

costs.amount: Not yet settled in published guidance
costs.note: This category is new. Verify current fees directly with the Immigration Department or through counsel before budgeting.

pathways.timeline: Unsettled. Treat published timelines with scepticism until implementing regulations and a track record exist.

steps.title: Confirm the category is operational for your profile today
steps.detail: The law took effect 1 July 2026, but detailed implementing regulations were still emerging. Ask the sponsor's counsel what has actually been granted, not what the law permits.

steps.title: Have the sponsoring institution assess you against the high-quality personnel criteria
steps.detail: This is the gate. It is an institutional judgement, not a self-assessment.

steps.title: Run the standard document authentication in parallel
steps.detail: Degrees, employment history, and criminal record will be needed on any route. Do this work regardless of which category you end on.

steps.title: Keep the work permit route open as your fallback
steps.detail: Until UĐ1 has a visible track record, treat it as an upgrade on a work permit plan, not a replacement for one.

failureModes.mistake: Reading UĐ1 as a digital nomad visa
failureModes.consequence: Months spent pursuing a category you cannot enter without an institutional sponsor.
failureModes.avoid: If no Vietnamese institution will name you, this route is closed.

failureModes.mistake: Abandoning a viable work permit application to wait for UĐ1
failureModes.consequence: You lose a working route for an unproven one.
failureModes.avoid: Run them in sequence, not instead of each other.

verification.check: Whether UĐ1 visas are actually being granted yet, as opposed to merely legislated
verification.authority: Your sponsoring institution, and the Vietnam Immigration Department
verification.how: Ask the sponsor: "How many UĐ1 visas has this institution obtained, and what was the issue date of the most recent one?"
verification.expectAnswer: A number and a date. "We are looking into it" means this route is not yet operational for you — keep the work permit plan running.

verification.check: Whether the route from UĐ1 to a residence card has implementing regulations yet
verification.authority: Vietnam Immigration Department, via your sponsor
verification.how: Ask whether a UĐ1 holder can currently be issued a temporary residence card, and under which instrument.

pathways.name: DT Investor Visa and Residence Card
pathways.summary: Four tiers keyed to how much capital you actually contribute to a Vietnamese company. The tier determines everything, and only DT3 and above produce a residence card.
pathways.bestFor: People building a real Vietnamese business with meaningful capital. A poor fit for anyone forming a shell company purely to buy residency.
pathways.durationGranted: DT1: visa up to 5 years, residence card up to 10 years. DT2: up to 5 years, card up to 5. DT3: up to 3 years, card up to 3. DT4: visa up to 12 months, no residence card.
pathways.renewable: Yes, while the investment and the company remain in good standing.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: DT1 is the tier most often discussed alongside a long-term permanent residence horizon. Take specific legal advice rather than relying on marketing claims.
pathways.canBringFamily: Yes, dependants on TT status once you hold a residence card — which again means DT3 or above.
pathways.canWorkLocally: In your own invested company. Note that owners and board members above capital thresholds may also fall in a work permit exemption category.

eligibility.requirement: DT1: contributed capital of VND 100 billion or more, roughly US$3.8M
eligibility.detail: Or investment in a sector or area the government specifically encourages.

eligibility.requirement: DT2: VND 50 to under 100 billion, roughly US$1.9M to 3.8M
DT3: VND 3 to under 50 billion, roughly US$115k to 1.9M
eligibility.detail: The entry point for a residence card. Below this you are in DT4 and get no card.

eligibility.requirement: DT4: under VND 3 billion
eligibility.detail: Visa up to 12 months, no residence card. Read the reality check before choosing this.

eligibility.requirement: A real investment registration and actual capital contribution
eligibility.detail: Registered capital that is never contributed does not hold up. The capital must move and be evidenced.

costs.amount: VND 3 billion minimum for a residence card
costs.note: This is contributed capital in a Vietnamese company, not an escrow deposit you get back.

costs.item: Ongoing accounting, audit, and tax compliance
costs.note: The cost people forget. A Vietnamese company files monthly and annually whether or not it trades.

costs.amount: Roughly US$145 to 320 for the card

pathways.timeline: 3 to 6 months from decision to residence card, dominated by investment registration and getting capital properly contributed and evidenced.

steps.title: Decide the tier before you incorporate
steps.detail: The capital number drives the visa outcome. Incorporating first and discovering you are in DT4 is the classic and expensive error.

steps.title: Obtain the investment registration certificate and enterprise registration certificate
steps.detail: Two separate documents. Both are needed downstream.

steps.title: Open the direct investment capital account and actually transfer the capital
steps.detail: Capital must come in through the correct account type or it will not be recognised as contributed. Get this wrong and the money is in Vietnam but not counted.
steps.who: You, with your bank and counsel
steps.blocker: The visa application depends on evidenced contribution.

steps.title: Apply for the DT visa at the tier your contribution supports
steps.detail: The tier is assessed on what you actually contributed.

steps.title: Apply for the residence card if you are at DT3 or above
steps.detail: Same 5 to 10 working day processing as other card types.

failureModes.mistake: Registering large capital but contributing little
failureModes.consequence: Tier assessed on the contribution, not the registration. You paid for a company and got a 12-month visa.
failureModes.avoid: Only register capital you will genuinely transfer, and transfer it through the correct account.

failureModes.mistake: Ignoring ongoing compliance cost
failureModes.consequence: A dormant company accrues filing obligations and penalties, and a struck-off company takes your visa basis with it.
failureModes.avoid: Budget annual compliance from day one.

failureModes.mistake: Believing an agency that says VND 3 billion is not really required
failureModes.consequence: DT4, no card, and no refund.
failureModes.avoid: The tier boundaries are published. Ask the agency to point at the decree.

verification.check: Which capital tier your planned contribution actually lands in
verification.authority: The Department of Planning and Investment (Sở Kế hoạch và Đầu tư) of the province you will register in
verification.how: Present your intended contributed capital figure and ask which DT tier it supports and whether a temporary residence card is available at that tier.
verification.expectAnswer: A tier and a yes or no on the residence card. Get this before you incorporate, not after.

verification.check: That your capital will be recognised as contributed
verification.how: Ask the bank to confirm in writing that the account you are wiring into is a direct investment capital account and that transfers to it will count as contributed charter capital.
verification.expectAnswer: Written confirmation naming the account type. Money in the wrong account type can fail to count.

pathways.name: DH Student Visa
pathways.summary: Sponsored by the institution that admitted you. A legitimate, low-cost way to hold lawful long-term status while you build the Vietnamese language ability and network that make the other routes viable.
pathways.bestFor: Younger movers, career changers, and anyone treating a first year in Vietnam as an investment in optionality.
pathways.durationGranted: Aligned to the program, typically up to 1 year at a time, with a residence card possible for longer programs.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: No, but it builds continuous lawful residence and local credentials.
pathways.canBringFamily: Limited. Do not plan a family move around this route.
pathways.canWorkLocally: No. Student status is not work authorisation, and the tourist-visa reasoning about remote work applies here too.

eligibility.requirement: Admission to an institution licensed to host foreign students
eligibility.detail: Universities and accredited full-time language programs. A part-time evening class at a private centre generally cannot sponsor you.

eligibility.requirement: Proof of funds and accommodation
eligibility.detail: Requirements are set by the institution and vary widely.

eligibility.requirement: Authenticated prior academic records
eligibility.detail: Same apostille and translation pipeline as the work permit route.

costs.note: University degree programs cost more; still well below US equivalents.

costs.amount: US$145 to 320 for a card, less for visa-only status

pathways.timeline: 6 to 12 weeks from admission to visa in hand.

steps.title: Secure admission from a licensed institution
steps.detail: Confirm in writing that they sponsor DH visas for foreign students, and ask how many they issued last year.
steps.blocker: Nothing proceeds without the admission letter.

steps.title: Authenticate prior academic records
steps.detail: Apostille and certified translation.

steps.title: The institution sponsors the visa
steps.detail: Filed by the school, not by you.

steps.title: Enter, declare temporary residence, and apply for the card if the program supports one
steps.detail: Standard 12-hour accommodation declaration on arrival.

failureModes.mistake: Enrolling at a private language centre that cannot sponsor
failureModes.consequence: You paid tuition and got no status.
failureModes.avoid: Confirm sponsorship capability in writing before paying.

failureModes.mistake: Taking paid work on student status
failureModes.consequence: Same illegal employment exposure as the tourist visa case.
failureModes.avoid: Keep income sources outside Vietnam, or convert to a work permit.

verification.check: That the institution can actually sponsor a DH visa
verification.how: Ask how many DH student visas they sponsored in the last year, and ask to be put in contact with a current foreign student.
verification.expectAnswer: A number and a contact. Vagueness here usually means they cannot sponsor and expect you to arrange your own status.

modules.title: Decide and pressure-test
modules.intro: Before you spend a dollar. The goal of this phase is to kill bad plans cheaply.

items.task: Run the decision tree and write down your pathway id
items.detail: Everything else in this guide filters on it.

items.task: Confirm your pathway is open to you on your worst-case facts
items.detail: Assume the job offer falls through, the capital is 20% short, the marriage paperwork is slower than promised. Does a route still exist?
items.why: Almost all relocation failures are single-point-of-failure plans.

items.task: Take a 2 to 4 week scouting trip on a 90-day e-visa
items.detail: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City are different countries for your purposes. Da Nang is a third. Spend real time before committing.
items.why: The cost of the trip is trivial against the cost of moving to the wrong city.

items.task: Check your passport expiry today
items.detail: If it has under 2 years remaining, renew it before anything else. Vietnamese residence cards must expire at least 30 days before your passport, so a short passport gives you a short card.

items.task: Price the real annual cost, not the blog cost
items.detail: Include health insurance, visa and card renewals, flights home, and — if you are on the investor route — annual company compliance.

items.task: Decide what would make you leave
items.detail: Write it down now, while you are calm. A named trigger prevents both sunk-cost paralysis and panic exits.

modules.title: Assemble and authenticate documents
modules.intro: This phase, not the visa application, is what actually determines your timeline. US document authentication is slow, sequential, and unforgiving.

items.task: Understand the apostille switchover before ordering anything
items.detail: The Hague Apostille Convention enters into force for Vietnam on 11 September 2026. From that date, US public documents need a single apostille instead of the old multi-step consular legalization through a Vietnamese mission.
items.why: Ordering the wrong form of authentication wastes 4 to 8 weeks and the fees are not refundable.

items.task: List every document your pathway needs, with its issuing authority
items.detail: Typically: degree, FBI Identity History Summary, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates. Federal documents are apostilled by the US Department of State; state-issued documents by that state's Secretary of State.

items.task: Time the FBI Identity History Summary deliberately
items.detail: It must be under 6 months old when filed. Order it via an FBI-approved channeler for a days-long turnaround rather than weeks, and work backwards from your employer's filing date.
items.why: Ordering it too early fails exactly like ordering it too late.

items.task: Order extra certified copies of everything
items.detail: Two or three of each. You will need originals in more than one place, and reordering from abroad is miserable.

items.task: Get certified Vietnamese translations
items.detail: Use a translation office that routinely handles immigration filings — they know the formatting the authorities expect.

items.task: Scan everything to encrypted cloud storage before you ship or carry it
items.detail: Full colour, both sides, including the authentication certificates themselves.

items.task: Do not authenticate the health certificate abroad
items.detail: The health check is normally done at a licensed hospital in Vietnam after arrival.

modules.title: Close out the United States
modules.intro: The US side of the move. Being a US citizen abroad is an ongoing legal relationship, not a departure.

items.task: Understand that you keep filing US taxes forever
items.detail: The US taxes citizens on worldwide income regardless of where they live. Moving to Vietnam does not end your filing obligation; it complicates it.

items.task: Learn the FEIE and FTC basics before you pick a strategy
items.detail: For tax year 2026 the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion tops out at US$132,900 per person, claimed on Form 2555, and requires either the Physical Presence Test of 330 full days abroad in a 12-month period or the Bona Fide Residence Test. It covers earned income only — not dividends, interest, rent, or capital gains.

items.task: Know that there is no US-Vietnam tax treaty in force
items.detail: The 2015 treaty was signed and ratified by Vietnam but never by the US Senate. There are no tie-breaker rules for dual residency and no reduced withholding. Since Vietnam taxes residents on worldwide income at rates up to 35%, the Foreign Tax Credit is usually the stronger long-term tool for higher earners.

items.task: Plan your FBAR compliance
items.detail: FinCEN Form 114 is required if your foreign accounts together exceeded US$10,000 at any point in the year, even for a single day. A Vietnamese salary account crosses this quickly.

items.task: Decide your state domicile deliberately
items.detail: Some states keep taxing you after you leave the country if you keep ties. Handle the driver's licence, voter registration, and mailing address as one coherent decision, not three accidents.
items.why: State residency disputes are the most common unpleasant surprise for new expats.

items.task: Set up a mail forwarding service with scanning
items.detail: A real street address, not a PO box — many financial institutions reject PO boxes.

items.task: Tell your banks and brokerages before you go
items.detail: Some close accounts on a foreign address; others freeze on foreign logins. Find out which yours is while you can still walk into a branch.

items.task: Understand that Medicare does not cover you in Vietnam
items.detail: Medicare generally does not pay for care outside the US. Budget for international or local health insurance from day one.

items.task: Confirm Social Security payments abroad if relevant
items.detail: Benefits are generally payable to US citizens in Vietnam, but the reporting and direct deposit setup differ. Handle it before you leave.

items.task: Register for absentee voting
items.detail: Through the Federal Voting Assistance Program, using your last US voting address.

items.task: Sort pets early if you have them
items.detail: Import requirements, airline crate rules, and summer heat embargoes each independently kill moves. Start 4 to 6 months out.

items.task: Decide between shipping and replacing
items.detail: Sea freight to Vietnam runs 6 to 10 weeks. Most household goods are cheaper to rebuy locally; ship what is irreplaceable, not what is expensive.

modules.title: Money and banking
modules.intro: Vietnam is substantially a cash economy in daily life and a heavily documented one in official life. Both facts matter.

items.task: Keep a US bank account open, permanently
items.detail: You will need it for US tax refunds, brokerage links, and card payments to US services. Closing it is very hard to reverse from abroad.

items.task: Get cards with no foreign transaction fee before you leave
items.detail: Applying for US credit from a Vietnamese address is close to impossible.

items.task: Plan how you will move money and at what cost
items.detail: Compare a specialist transfer service against your bank's wire on a realistic monthly amount. The spread matters more than the fee.

items.task: Understand the investor capital account rule if you are on the DT route
items.detail: Investment capital must enter through the correct direct investment capital account or it may not count as contributed. Do not wire it to a personal account.

items.task: Open a Vietnamese bank account once you have status and an address
items.detail: Requirements tighten and loosen; a residence card and a lease make it straightforward, a tourist visa often does not.

items.task: Budget the compulsory insurance cost if you are employed locally
items.detail: Foreign employees on local contracts of 12 months or more with a valid work permit fall under compulsory social insurance. Total contributions run about 30% of salary, with roughly 20.5% from the employer and 9.5% from the employee. Foreigners do not pay unemployment insurance, which is why the total is 2 points below the Vietnamese rate.

modules.title: Arrival week
modules.intro: A short list, but one item on it has a 12-hour deadline.

items.task: Enter at the exact port named on your e-visa
items.detail: If your routing changed, you needed a new e-visa before boarding.

items.task: Confirm your temporary residence declaration was actually filed
items.detail: The accommodation provider — hotel, landlord, or employer — must declare your presence to local police within 12 hours of your arrival at the accommodation, 24 hours in remote areas, using form NA17. Registration is free. Hotels do it automatically; private landlords often do not.
items.why: Failure exposes the host to fines of several million VND, and a missing declaration surfaces later as a gap when you apply for a residence card.

items.task: Get a local SIM with a proper registration
items.detail: Bring your passport. An unregistered number will fail verification for banking and government apps.

items.task: Do not sign a 12-month lease in your first week
items.detail: Take a month somewhere serviced. Neighbourhood mistakes are expensive and hard to unwind.

items.task: Photograph your entry stamp
items.detail: It is the start date for your permitted stay and for tax residency counting.

items.task: Start counting days for tax residency from arrival
items.detail: 183 days in a calendar year, or in 12 consecutive months from your first arrival, makes you a Vietnamese tax resident on worldwide income.

modules.title: First 90 days
modules.intro: Converting arrival into residence. Most of this runs in parallel; start all of it in week two.

items.task: Complete the Vietnamese health certificate
items.detail: At a licensed hospital. Half a day.

items.task: File the residence card application
items.detail: Processing is typically 5 to 10 working days, with online submission available since 2025. Fees run roughly US$145 to 320 depending on validity.

items.task: Sign a lease with your name on it and get the landlord's tax and ownership documents
items.detail: You need a lease in your own name for banking, residence registration, and often the residence card itself.

items.task: Confirm the landlord re-files your temporary residence declaration for the new address
items.detail: It is per-accommodation, not once per country.

items.task: Convert your US driver's licence
items.detail: You may convert once you have been resident about three months and hold a residence card or equivalent with at least 3 months validity. You need a notarised Vietnamese translation of the US licence plus passport and visa copies. The Vietnamese licence issued matches the class of the US one — a car-only US licence will not convert into a motorbike licence.
items.why: Riding without a valid licence voids most travel and health insurance after an accident. Motorbike accidents are the single largest health risk to foreigners in Vietnam.

items.task: Buy health insurance that actually covers medical evacuation
items.detail: Serious trauma and complex surgery are frequently handled by evacuation to Bangkok or Singapore. Check the evacuation limit, not just the annual maximum.

items.task: Open the Vietnamese bank account
items.detail: Bring passport, residence card, and lease.

items.task: Register with the US Embassy or Consulate
items.detail: Through the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program, so you receive alerts and can be contacted in an emergency.

items.task: Start Vietnamese lessons in month one
items.detail: The gap between foreigners who are content in Vietnam long term and those who leave at eighteen months correlates with this more than with income.

modules.title: Staying legal, year after year
modules.intro: Vietnamese status is a renewal treadmill. Build a calendar in your first month and never rely on an employer to remember for you.

items.task: Calendar every expiry with a 90-day and 60-day alert
items.detail: Passport, visa, residence card, work permit, driving licence, insurance. Put them in one place.

items.task: Start work permit and residence card renewals 60 to 90 days out
items.detail: The residence card cannot outlast the work permit, and both must clear before the current card expires.

items.task: Renew your US passport when it hits 2 years remaining
items.detail: Because the residence card must expire at least 30 days before the passport, a short passport truncates your card at every renewal.

items.task: File your Vietnamese personal income tax
items.detail: Residents are taxed on worldwide employment income at progressive rates from 5% to 35% under the five-bracket schedule applying from the 2026 tax year, with a personal deduction of VND 15.5 million per month and VND 6.2 million per dependant. Non-residents pay a flat 20% on Vietnam-sourced employment income.

items.task: File your US return and FBAR every year
items.detail: Expats get an automatic extension to 15 June, but interest still runs from April. FBAR is separate from the tax return.

items.task: Coordinate the two tax systems deliberately, once, with a professional
items.detail: With no treaty in force, the interaction of Vietnamese worldwide taxation and US citizenship taxation is genuinely complex. One session with an accountant who handles both is the highest-return money in this guide.

items.task: Re-declare temporary residence whenever you move address
items.detail: Every new accommodation, every time, within 12 hours.

items.task: Keep a document folder that a lawyer could pick up cold
items.detail: Entry stamps, every visa and card, leases, tax filings, work permits. Continuity of lawful residence is proven with paper.

modules.title: Contingency and exit
modules.window: Have this before you need it
modules.intro: Written while things are going well, so that it exists when they are not.

items.task: Know what happens to your status if you lose your job
items.detail: Your work permit and residence card are tied to the sponsoring employer. Losing the job starts a clock. Ask your employer's HR exactly what that clock is before you need the answer.

items.task: Keep 3 months of expenses plus a one-way flight home, liquid
items.detail: In an account you can reach from either country.

items.task: Know the overstay process before you ever overstay
items.detail: Overstay is resolved with fines and an exit procedure, and it leaves a record that makes future applications harder. It is not the end of the world, and it is also not nothing.

items.task: Keep US documents current while abroad
items.detail: Passport, and a valid US driver's licence if you might return.

items.task: Write your plan B pathway id
items.detail: If your current pathway closes, which node of the tree do you re-enter at? Answer it now.

gotchas.title: The apostille switchover lands on 11 September 2026
gotchas.trap: Vietnam acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention on 31 December 2025, and it enters into force for Vietnam on 11 September 2026. Documents authenticated the old way and the new way are both in circulation right now, and agencies are giving out instructions written for the old regime. Getting consular legalization when an apostille is required, or the reverse, wastes 4 to 8 weeks and non-refundable fees.
gotchas.doThis: For US public documents intended for use in Vietnam from 11 September 2026 onward, obtain a single apostille: US Department of State for federal documents such as the FBI Identity History Summary, and the relevant Secretary of State for state-issued documents like degrees and marriage certificates. Before you order anything, confirm with the specific Vietnamese authority that will receive the document which form they are accepting that week. Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs — the Consular Department in Hanoi and the Department of Foreign Affairs in Ho Chi Minh City — issues apostilles on the Vietnamese side.

gotchas.title: The FBI criminal record check has a 6-month shelf life
gotchas.trap: Work permit applications require a criminal record check issued within the last 6 months. Applicants order it as their very first task, then spend four months on job offers and degree authentication, and file with a document that is five and a half months old — or already expired.
gotchas.doThis: Fix the employer's filing date first. Order the FBI Identity History Summary through an approved channeler roughly 6 to 8 weeks before that date, then apostille it immediately.

gotchas.title: Your e-visa names one port of entry and means it
gotchas.trap: The e-visa carries a declared checkpoint. Arrive at a different airport or land border and you can be refused entry, with the airline liable for flying you back.
gotchas.doThis: Match the port to your actual ticket. If your routing changes — a rebooking through Hanoi instead of Ho Chi Minh City — apply for a new e-visa before you fly. US$25 is cheaper than a denied boarding.

gotchas.title: Your residence card must expire at least 30 days before your passport
gotchas.trap: People with 18 months left on a US passport apply for a 2-year residence card and receive a card truncated to about 17 months, then pay the full fee again the following year.
gotchas.doThis: Renew the US passport before applying for or renewing any Vietnamese residence card. Treat 2 years of remaining passport validity as your floor.

gotchas.title: Somebody must declare your address to the police within 12 hours
gotchas.trap: The obligation sits with the accommodation provider, so foreigners assume it is handled. Hotels do it automatically. Private landlords and friends whose spare room you are using very often do not. The declaration is free, uses form NA17, and its absence surfaces months later as a problem in a residence card application.
gotchas.doThis: Ask the landlord directly, in the first 12 hours, whether the declaration has been filed, and ask for confirmation. Repeat at every address change. Non-compliance exposes the host to fines in the millions of VND.

gotchas.title: The 183-day line makes you taxable on worldwide income
gotchas.trap: Presence for 183 days in a calendar year, or across 12 consecutive months from first arrival, makes you a Vietnamese tax resident on worldwide income at rates up to 35%. A habitual residence — a registered address or a fixed-term lease — can also make you resident. Americans arriving in August often assume the first partial year is free. The rolling 12-month test says otherwise.
gotchas.doThis: Count days from your first entry stamp, and get advice before your first 183rd day, not after. With no US-Vietnam treaty in force, there are no tie-breaker rules to rescue a dual-residency position.

gotchas.title: Under VND 3 billion, the investor route gives you no residence card
gotchas.trap: DT4 — capital under VND 3 billion — grants a visa of up to 12 months and no temporary residence card. Formation agencies quote the incorporation fee, not the residency outcome.
gotchas.doThis: If residency is the goal, the number to clear is VND 3 billion in genuinely contributed capital, entering at DT3. If you cannot clear it, solve residence a different way and decide on the company purely as a business question.

gotchas.title: Nobody can sell you a Vietnamese golden visa
gotchas.trap: A 5-to-10-year golden visa was proposed in 2025 and has been reported worldwide as though it launched. As of this guide's verification date there is no decree and no application channel. Some sites cite a 'Resolution 41/2026/QH15' that no government source confirms.
gotchas.doThis: If anyone offers to process a Vietnamese golden visa, ask for the decree number and the government portal. There is no correct answer they can give. Use the DT tiers or UĐ1 instead, both of which actually exist.

gotchas.title: Your work permit belongs to your employer, not to you
gotchas.trap: The permit names one employer and one position. Changing jobs does not carry it across, and the residence card built on it falls with it.
gotchas.doThis: Before accepting a new offer, confirm the new employer will file a fresh permit and understand the gap in between. Never resign before the new filing is in motion.

gotchas.title: A car licence does not convert into a motorbike licence
gotchas.trap: Conversion produces a Vietnamese licence of the same class as the US original. Most Americans hold car-only licences, then ride a motorbike anyway. After an accident, insurers decline on the licence class, and motorbike injuries are the largest single health risk to foreigners in Vietnam.
gotchas.doThis: If you intend to ride, obtain the motorbike category properly rather than assuming your car licence converts. Confirm your health and travel policies cover motorbike use at your licence class, in writing.

sources.title: Law No. 118/2025/QH15 amending 10 laws on security and public order — in force 1 July 2026; introduces UĐ1 and UĐ2 visas

contested.question: Does marriage to a Vietnamese citizen still exempt you from needing a work permit?

positions.position: It remains an exemption category. Being married to a Vietnamese citizen and residing in Vietnam was a listed work permit exemption under the previous Decree 152/2020 regime, and commentary on Decree 219/2025 generally treats the exemption list as carried over and clarified rather than narrowed.
positions.heldBy: Most law firm commentary on Decree 219/2025

positions.position: It cannot be assumed. Decree 219/2025 replaced Decree 152/2020 outright on 7 August 2025 and restated the exemption list; sources differ on whether there are roughly 15 or roughly 20 categories, which means the list was not simply copied across.
positions.heldBy: A conservative reading of the replacement decree

contested.practicalEffect: Do not start work on the assumption that you are exempt. Whichever reading is right, an exemption still requires a written confirmation before you begin — so the safe action is identical either way.
contested.howToResolve: Have your employer submit a written enquiry to the provincial labour authority asking which article of Decree 219/2025 covers spouses of Vietnamese citizens, then file for the written exemption confirmation citing it.

contested.question: Is remote work for a foreign employer on a Vietnamese e-visa illegal, or merely unpermitted?

positions.position: It is prohibited. Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law bars foreigners on a tourist entry from labour activities, and administrative fines of VND 15 to 25 million are provided for illegal employment.

It is a tolerated grey zone. Multiple long-running expat sources report effectively no enforcement against foreigners working online for clients outside Vietnam, and describe it as tolerated but not permitted.
positions.heldBy: Expat community reporting and practitioner commentary

contested.practicalEffect: Both readings agree on the facts and disagree only on the risk. You are relying on non-enforcement, not on a right, and non-enforcement can end without notice or transition. Decide with that stated plainly, and do not describe yourself as working when dealing with immigration.
contested.howToResolve: This one cannot be resolved by asking an official — no authority will confirm a tolerance in writing. If the risk is unacceptable to you, the resolution is structural: get a work permit, or invest at DT3 and above.

contested.question: Will Vietnam tax your worldwide income once you pass 183 days?

positions.position: Yes. Tax residents are subject to Vietnamese personal income tax on worldwide employment income at progressive rates up to 35%, regardless of where the income is paid.
positions.heldBy: Professional tax guidance on the regime applying from the 2026 tax year

positions.position: In practice, enforcement against foreign-sourced salary paid offshore to individuals with no Vietnamese employer is inconsistent, and many long-stayers have never been assessed.

contested.practicalEffect: Plan on the legal position, not the enforcement position. The cost of being wrong is back taxes and penalties in a country you live in, and with no US-Vietnam treaty in force there are no tie-breaker rules to fall back on.
contested.howToResolve: Take one paid session with an accountant who handles both US and Vietnamese filings, before your first 183rd day. This is the single highest-return professional spend of the whole move.

watchlist.title: Apostille replaces consular legalization for US documents
watchlist.whatChanges: Every document-authentication instruction in this pack switches from consular legalization to a single apostille. Once offices are demonstrably accepting apostilles in practice, the transition warning can be reduced to a plain instruction.

watchlist.title: UĐ1 and UĐ2 implementing regulations, including conversion to a residence card
watchlist.whatChanges: If a clear UĐ1-to-residence-card route is published, UĐ1 becomes a genuine primary pathway rather than an upgrade on a work permit, and its position in the decision tree moves ahead of the capital questions.

watchlist.title: The proposed 5-to-10 year golden visa
watchlist.whatChanges: If an actual decree with an application channel appears, this becomes a new pathway and a major reality-check entry is retired. Until a decree number exists, it stays in the reality check as a thing that does not exist.

watchlist.title: Enforcement posture toward remote workers on e-visas
watchlist.whatChanges: The dead-end advice for remote workers is calibrated to near-zero enforcement. Any visible enforcement action would change that from a tolerated risk to an unacceptable one, and the dead end would need rewriting.

watchlist.title: Personal income tax five-bracket schedule bedding in for the 2026 tax year
watchlist.whatChanges: Bracket boundaries and the VND 15.5 million monthly personal deduction should be reconfirmed against a filed return once the first full year under the new schedule has been assessed.
